summary: Tested agent Medicaid Provider editing (LeadDetail + SharedLeadDetail), hidden-field enforcement (UI pencil + backend strip), and owner-only Book of Business agent filter. Backend 9/9 pytest pass. UI: all requested flows pass. One permission/privacy gap found: GET /api/shared-leads/{id} (and PATCH responses) are NOT masked, so an agent with medicaid_provider hidden still SEES the value on SharedLeadDetail (no pencil, but value displayed).

minor.issue: Returns clean_doc(lead) without mask_lead_for_user, so hidden fields (medicaid_provider, phone, address...) are visible to agents on SharedLeadDetail. Verified: with medicaid_provider hidden, agent saw 'UISharedAgent' on /shared-leads/{id}. Same for PATCH /api/shared-leads/{id} response. GET /api/shared-leads list 'plan' column also exposes medicaid_provider.
Response returns unmasked doc (clean_doc) to agents — hidden field values leak in the PATCH response body (UI then may setLead with them). Wrap with mask_lead_for_user.
can_access_shared_pool=False is only enforced on the list endpoint; an agent with pool access disabled can still lock/view/edit a shared lead by id (pre-existing).
BoB Export CSV button uses ?status=Complete only — ignores the new agent filter (and q/effective filters).

ui_bugs.issue: 'Assigned to 4aafe7e8-...' shows raw agent UUID instead of agent name when logged in as agent

issues: Medicaid Provider row (TapEditField) has no leading icon unlike other InfoRows, slight misalignment
Subtitle 'the ones you closed' is odd for owner viewing all/other agents
When filtered by agent, 'Completed by' column shows completer (Test Owner) not the assigned agent; consider showing Agent column

action_items: Apply mask_lead_for_user in GET /api/shared-leads/{id} and in PATCH /api/shared-leads/{id} + PATCH /api/leads/{id} responses so hidden fields are not shown to agents
Optional: pass agent_id (and other filters) to BoB Export CSV
Optional: show agent name instead of UUID in LeadDetail 'Assigned to' for agents
Optional: enforce can_access_shared_pool on lock/get/patch shared-lead endpoints
critical_code_review_comments: strip_hidden_fields correctly applied in both PATCH endpoints; owner bypass correct; legacy users (visible_fields None) allowed
GET /leads agent_id filter correctly owner-only; agents passing agent_id still scoped to own leads (verified)
Frontend canEdit relies on AuthContext user; if owner changes visible_fields while agent is logged in, pencil stays until /auth/me refetch (backend still strips, so safe)

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows; 1 masking leak found on SharedLeadDetail

seed_data_creation: TEST_ leads created and deleted. agent1 visible_fields restored to full list; agent1 can_access_shared_pool was False before testing, temporarily set True for UI, restored to False.

Use iter12_ui_setup.py (setup/hide/restore/pool_on/pool_off/teardown). Run pytest with -n 0 (xdist is enabled in pytest.ini).
